knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson requires the facts to be recorded, the matter dealt with through the procedure, and the worker protected from retaliation. Dismissing it as personal (option 0) and telling the worker to stop complaining (option 2) are the errors the lesson names.

The lesson says protected attributes come from the applicable Commonwealth, state or territory law, which must be checked for the location. The business's preference (option 0) and customer opinion (option 2) do not decide protection.
The discrimination and harassment section says discrimination is treating a person less favourably because of an attribute the law protects.

practicalCriteria: Learner records the facts of a supplied concern about unfair treatment and identifies the designated contact to tell.
Learner allocates a supplied set of shifts and tasks on the basis of the work and the rules, and records the basis.
Learner states what protection a worker who raised a concern in good faith must receive, and does not retaliate in the role-play.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Complaint record with facts, action taken and outcome
Record of work allocation decisions where the business keeps one
stopWorkCriteria: Learner dismisses a concern raised in good faith
Learner retaliates against a worker who raised a concern
